method: Filesystem search under lib/emsenn (excluding node_modules, lib/legacy, content/assets/legacy, _archive, apps/metroplat, and this section's own data/storage of published tarballs) for filenames matching *a2a-face*, *mcp-face*, *activitypub-face*, serve-activitypub*, activitypub-server*, activitypub-offer*, activitypub-runtime*, activitypub-network*, *agent-card*, serve-mcp*, *mcp-server*, *-mcp.mjs/.mts, mcp.mjs/.mts -- restricted to non-test source files. Each hit's nearest ancestor package.json gave its publishing package. Import statements in each hit were read to determine whether it composes a canonical a2a-services-section / activitypub-services-section package or reimplements protocol logic locally. a2a-services-section's own 14 services and their package.json exports were read first (see canonicalSection.services below) to serve as the comparison baseline. A broader, looser textual grep (agent-card, activitypub, AgentCard.fromJSON, tools/list, 'signed A2A', serveActivityPubProvider) across the same exclusions returned several hundred file references, but the great majority of those are legitimate consumers (clients fetching a well-known agent-card URL, tests, or correct composition of the canonical activitypub-services-section package) rather than embedded protocol-face implementations; that looser count is likely the source of the owner's 'hundreds' impression. The filename-based search above, restricted to files that plausibly *implement* a face, is the precise basis for this inventory's hits array.

paymentsExecuted.divergenceFound: Real, load-bearing divergence found and NOT forced: activitypub-services-section's canonical createActivityPubR2Custody deliberately exports no message queue (R2 has no atomic dequeue; its own source comment says so), whereas notebooklm's local ./activitypub-r2-custody.mjs bundles a hand-rolled R2-polling queue that serveActivityPubProvider requires (it throws without one outside test mode) and that this same file's production CLI entrypoint (bin: serve-notebooklm-activitypub) depends on at boot. github's precedent instead injects an unrelated, already-provisioned GCP Cloud Tasks queue for that role, which has no notebooklm-infrastructure equivalent (notebooklm is Cloudflare R2-only) and would be a new package/new infrastructure choice, out of scope. Resolution: ./activitypub-r2-custody.mjs was kept (still used unmodified by src/serve-cloud-run.mjs) and given one additional named export, createNotebookLmActivityPubR2Queue, isolating the exact same pre-existing queue implementation so serve-activitypub.mjs can compose canonical kv+inbox with it explicitly rather than pulling all three from the local hand-rolled custody.
